assets.prompt: Create a polished photographic educational comparison board for an English motion-capture tutorial. Portrait canvas, two equal columns and three rows, exactly six photo panels, subtle dark charcoal gutters. Only text at top: left column DON'T, right column DO, small clear sans-serif white text, red underline for DON'T, mint underline for DO. No other words, no logos, no diagrams or skeleton overlays. Same fictional average adult male dancer with short dark hair and medium skin in every panel, neutral gray studio background and visible floor. Each row shows a paired bad and good recording setup. TOP LEFT: dancer walks out of the recording area, most of his body outside the left edge and one cut-off arm/leg remain visible, clear negative example of leaving the frame. TOP RIGHT: same person fully visible head to shoes in center with ample empty margins while taking a side step, simple fitted navy T-shirt, gray athletic trousers, shoes. MIDDLE LEFT: same fully clothed dancer performing an arm movement, heavy camera-shake double edges and motion blur across body and hands, photograph visibly smeared and unusable; not an extra limb, just motion ghosting. MIDDLE RIGHT: same movement crisply frozen with stable framing and bright even lighting, all limbs and fingers as visible as possible, full body and floor. BOTTOM LEFT: full-body dancer wearing an oversized long bulky coat and scarf layered over loose trousers, sleeves covering hands, body outline and joints obscured by clothing. BOTTOM RIGHT: same person in simple fitted navy T-shirt and gray athletic trousers, hands uncovered, arms separated from torso, feet visible. Professional realistic instructional photos, consistent camera distance for good examples, clear silhouettes, natural anatomy. These are synthetic teaching examples, not product screenshots. Avoid nudity, brands, decorative text, extra people. Large high-quality output suitable for zooming on a website.

Create a professional photorealistic educational comparison board for an English avatar pose-photo tutorial. Square or slightly portrait canvas, exactly TWO columns and TWO rows, four photos with dark charcoal gutters. At top only: DON'T over left column with coral underline, DO over right column with mint underline. No other lettering, no logos, no skeleton overlays. Same fictional adult woman in all four panels, dark tied-back hair, olive skin, comfortable fitted teal long-sleeve athletic shirt, charcoal athletic trousers and sneakers, plain neutral gray photographic studio with floor. TOP LEFT is a BAD reference: person standing with left arm raised, but the photograph is cropped below knees and the raised hand cut off at the top; framing too tight to see the pose. TOP RIGHT is the GOOD version: the same pose, full body head to both shoes completely visible, raised hand fully visible, centered with generous margins all around, clear focus and even lighting. BOTTOM LEFT is a BAD reference: full-body person turned almost sideways, with overlapping bent arms crossing tightly in front of torso, hands hidden behind opposite elbows, far leg obscured by near leg; pose hard to read from the single photo. BOTTOM RIGHT is GOOD: full-body at a slight front three-quarter angle, legs apart, both bent arms held visibly away from the torso with hands uncovered and separated, elbows, knees, and feet easy to distinguish. Maintain realistic natural anatomy, consistent single person, no exaggerated contortions. Visually communicate clear photographic reference quality rather than attractiveness. High-quality photo board for a website guide, with clear small-screen readability. No nudity, brands, extra people or props.
